title: A closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by one element, or by a single nonzerodivisor, is locally principal, respectively an effective Cartier divisor

standard_prerequisites.name: The localization of a finitely generated ideal at a prime is generated by the localizations of its generators, and a principal generator at the prime can be written with denominators outside the prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a neighbourhood on which the ideal becomes principal, giving the first part.

standard_prerequisites.name: An element whose image in a localization at a prime is a nonzerodivisor is a nonzerodivisor on a neighbourhood of the prime, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the pointwise nonzerodivisor condition to a neighbourhood condition, giving the second part.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine neighbourhood: at a point of the closed subscheme pass to an affine chart and let the defining ideal be generated by finitely many elements, since the coordinate ring is Noetherian (proof lines 2954-2958).

Locally principal case: if the localized ideal at the prime is generated by a single element, write each generator as a multiple of it and clear the finitely many denominators appearing both in those multiples and in the generator; after inverting the product of the denominators the ideal becomes principal, which gives local principality (proof lines 2958-2967).

Effective Cartier case: under the stronger pointwise assumption that the ideal is generated by a single nonzerodivisor, one may assume the ideal is principal on the chart and the generator's image at the prime is a nonzerodivisor, whence by the cited statement the generator is a nonzerodivisor on a neighbourhood, so the closed subscheme is an effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 2968-2972).
proof_roadmap: Work on an affine chart and show that a pointwise principal ideal becomes principal after inverting finitely many elements, giving local principality (proof lines 2954-2967).
In the stronger case use the neighbourhood statement for regular elements to make the generator a nonzerodivisor locally, giving the Cartier property (proof lines 2968-2972).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a closed subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme, an ideal sheaf which is generated by one element at every point of the subscheme is locally principal, and one generated by a single nonzerodivisor at every point is an effective Cartier divisor (statement lines 2938-2952). The counted proof is short and complete: over an affine chart it uses Noetherianity to write the ideal by finitely many elements, converts the pointwise principal generation into a principal generation after inverting the finitely many denominators involved, and in the stronger case invokes the neighbourhood statement for regular elements to obtain the nonzerodivisor condition locally (proof lines 2954-2972). It is H2: both parts are carried out in the counted span, with the cited input being the standard neighbourhood statement for nonzerodivisors.
